lead.zh-Hans: 进门以前和进门以后，我各停了一小会儿。
lead.en: I paused once before the door, and once beyond it.

text.zh-Hans: 在墨西哥城美术宫，我先看白色大理石的外立面，再进去慢慢看。介绍里写着外部的新艺术风格和内部的装饰艺术风格，我把两个名字记在便纸的两面。出门时翻了一下纸，发现自己还没写最先注意到什么。明天想把进门前后的那一眼补上。
text.en: At the Palacio de Bellas Artes, I looked at the white-marble facade before taking my time inside. The introduction paired an Art Nouveau exterior with an Art Deco interior. I put one name on each side of a note. Leaving, I realized I had recorded the names but not what caught my eye first. Tomorrow I would like to add those two first impressions.

text.zh-Hans: 说说你先注意到了什么
text.en: Say what caught your eye first

text.zh-Hans: 记下进门前后的颜色
text.en: Keep a color from before and after the door

lead.zh-Hans: 查普尔特佩克的树下，碰面比约好时慢了一点。
lead.en: Our meeting beneath the trees took a little longer.

text.zh-Hans: 墨西哥城的查普尔特佩克是一片分为四区的城市森林。我和旅人约了在入口会合，走近才发现，彼此都先停下来整理了一次背包。等到终于碰头，谁也没催谁。我们沿路慢慢走，我把先听见招呼、后看见挥手的那一刻记在小纸上。
text.en: Chapultepec is a Mexico City urban forest with four sections. A traveler and I arranged to meet at an entrance. It turned out that both of us had stopped to rearrange a backpack. Once we met, neither was in a hurry. My small note keeps the moment when I heard the greeting just before I spotted the wave.

text.zh-Hans: 聊聊刚才各自在忙什么
text.en: Compare what kept each of you busy

text.zh-Hans: 想想招呼与挥手的先后
text.en: Recall the greeting just before the wave

lead.zh-Hans: 今天先学会一个菜名，再让午饭接着说。
lead.en: I learned a dish name, then let lunch do the talking.

text.zh-Hans: 在墨西哥城吃篮子塔可，我选了土豆馅。记菜单时，我把菜名慢慢念给同行旅人听，又指了指自己这份午饭。念到一半肚子先催了，我就把整句话缩成一个笑脸。吃完再补名字，这回总算记住菜单上谁先到、谁后到了。
text.en: I chose potato-filled tacos de canasta in Mexico City. While making a menu, I tried saying the dish’s name to a companion and pointed to my lunch. Hunger interrupted halfway through, so the speech became a small smile. I added the name after eating. Now I remember exactly which arrived first: lunch, then the sentence.

text.zh-Hans: 把菜名慢慢再说一遍
text.en: Try the dish name once more, slowly

text.zh-Hans: 看看菜单上名字和笑脸
text.en: Find the name and smile on the menu

lead.zh-Hans: 午饭像个小包裹，要先打开才好说话。
lead.en: Lunch arrived as a little parcel of its own.

text.zh-Hans: 在墨西哥城买了一份玉米苞叶包的塔马尔，里面是玉米面团和馅料。我坐稳了，慢慢展开外面的叶子，原先想写的开头也跟着慢了一点。后来在菜单上记了两步：先打开，再尝一口。不是做菜的方法，只是今天午饭找到我的顺序。
text.en: My Mexico City tamal came wrapped in a corn husk, with corn dough and filling inside. Settled in my seat, I unwrapped it slowly, and my planned opening sentence slowed down too. The menu has two steps: open, then taste. No cooking instructions, just the order in which lunch reached me.

text.zh-Hans: 说说打开午饭时想到什么
text.en: Tell what the little parcel brought to mind

text.zh-Hans: 留意展开前后的样子
text.en: Notice the change as the wrapping opens

lead.zh-Hans: 两个菜名，今天都有了自己的座位。
lead.en: Both dish names found a place at the table today.

text.zh-Hans: 我和旅人说起墨西哥城吃过的篮子塔可与塔马尔，把两张菜单放在面前。一个让我想起土豆馅的那顿午饭，一个让我想起慢慢展开的玉米苞叶。我先说名字，再讲自己的小事；说完以后，两个名字就不再只是一串等我认的字了。
text.en: I laid out the tacos de canasta and tamales menus while talking with a traveler in Mexico City. One returned me to my potato-filled lunch, the other to the corn husk opening slowly. I said each name, then told the small memory that belonged to it. The words felt much easier to recognize afterwards.

text.zh-Hans: 给两顿午饭各讲一小段
text.en: Give each lunch its own short story

text.zh-Hans: 看看哪个名字先被记住
text.en: See which name comes back first

lead.zh-Hans: 两顿午饭，开头的动作不太一样。
lead.en: Two lunches began with different little movements.

text.zh-Hans: 收好墨西哥城的两张菜单前，我又看了一遍。篮子塔可那张留着一个没说完菜名的笑脸，塔马尔那张记着打开苞叶的顺序。我在纸背各写一句回想，然后把菜单并排放好。今天记住的除了味道，还有自己怎样安安稳稳坐下来吃饭。
text.en: Before putting away my Mexico City menus, I looked once more. The tacos card keeps a smile where the dish name went unfinished; the tamal card recalls opening the husk. I wrote a memory on each back and laid them together. Alongside the tastes, I had kept the small movements of settling down to eat.

text.zh-Hans: 说说哪顿饭先浮上心头
text.en: Say which lunch returns to mind first

text.zh-Hans: 翻到纸背看看两种开头
text.en: Turn the cards over to revisit the beginnings

lead.zh-Hans: 你说“{reply}”，这张便纸终于有了我的那一眼。
lead.en: You suggested “{reply},” and the note finally acquired my own first impressions.

text.zh-Hans: 我把墨西哥城美术宫那张双面便签取出来，先记白色大理石外墙，再记自己进门时注意到的色彩。颜色只照着这次记忆写，没有替整座建筑下结论。我把便签折进一张小卡，翻开能从门外走到门里，合上又回到当天出门的那一刻。
text.en: I took out my two-sided note from the Palacio de Bellas Artes. First came the white marble outside; then the colors I remembered noticing beyond the door. They describe my visit, rather than the whole building. Tucked into a small card, the note opens from outside to inside and closes on the moment I left.

text.zh-Hans: 给翻开的卡讲一句开头
text.en: Give the opening card a first sentence

text.zh-Hans: 翻一翻门外与门里的两面
text.en: Turn between the outside and inside

lead.zh-Hans: 墨西哥城的这一餐，我从外面慢慢打开。
lead.en: Unwrapping lunch slowly in Mexico City.

text.zh-Hans: 塔马尔吃完了，玉米苞叶还摊在面前。我试着沿折痕把它包回原样，少了里面的玉米面团和馅料，怎么折都扁扁的。又到墨西哥城，我倒在收拾一顿饭时耽搁了很久。身旁的旅人看出我在忙什么，也帮着比了比，最后都笑了。叶子还是空的，今天的午餐已经装进了肚子，没法再包回去。我把桌面收干净，再写这封信。
text.en: The tamal was finished, but its corn husk lay open in front of me. I tried folding it back along its creases. Without the filled corn dough inside, it would not regain its shape. I had come all this way to Mexico City again, and now I was puzzling over an empty lunch wrapper. A fellow traveller tried to help; eventually we both laughed. The husk was empty and lunch was in my stomach, well beyond rewrapping. I cleared my place before writing to you.

text.zh-Hans: 聊聊包不回去的午餐
text.en: Talk about the unwrappable lunch

text.zh-Hans: 看看苞叶留下的折痕
text.en: Look at the creases in the husk
